reasons: The packet shows no tests for this file.
Some section labels in the packet do not match the code they cover, which makes review harder.
Cancellation relies on polling a marker file, so timing is approximate.

terms.meaning: a plain text format for storing structured data
one processing run started by an upload
saved results from an earlier run that can be reused for the same input
a small database kept in a single file
a fingerprint built from the file and version numbers, used to look up cached results
an empty file named cancel that tells running work to stop
a Python class that checks that data has the expected fields and types

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and version links
sections.what: Brings in tools for files, threads, data models, the schedule reader and the cache helpers.
sections.why: Likely reason: shared building blocks used by the job store.
sections.watch_out: Changing the parser or rule version values changes which saved results are reused.

sections.name: JobState
sections.title: Job status record shape
sections.what: Defines the saved status of a job: its ID, source name, status, progress counts, message, cache details, package details and timestamps. Unknown extra fields are rejected.
sections.why: Likely reason: a fixed shape makes a damaged or mismatched record fail loudly.
sections.watch_out: Renaming a field breaks reading of every saved state file written before the change.

sections.name: ModelArtifacts
sections.title: Project model file locations
sections.what: Holds the three file paths for one project's saved data: the model file, the staging database, and the attachment list.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeping the three paths together means every route finds them the same way.
sections.watch_out: Nothing here checks that the files exist, so a missing file only shows up when a route uses it.

sections.name: JobStore (part 1)
sections.title: Job folder setup and safety
sections.what: Creates the job store with its work and cache folders. Checks that a job ID contains only letters, digits and hyphens and that the job folder stays inside the work folder. Provides paths for the state, report and database files, and can delete a job.
sections.why: Likely reason: job IDs come from outside the program, so they are checked to block path tricks.
sections.watch_out: Any ID with other characters is refused before a file path is built, so the check must stay in place.

sections.name: JobStore: model_artifacts
sections.title: Resolving saved model locations
sections.what: Gives the file paths for one project's model. For package jobs it uses a committed generation folder and rejects IDs that are not 32 lowercase hex characters. For schedule jobs it uses files named by the project key.
sections.why: Likely reason: package models are versioned, so every consumer reads the same complete set.
sections.watch_out: A package project with no published generation raises a not-found error, and no older model is used in its place.

sections.name: JobStore: write
sections.title: Saving and loading job state
sections.what: Saves a job's status through a temporary file and a safe rename, and retries briefly if the file is locked. Keeps an in-memory copy. Loading reads memory first, then the disk, retrying a few times.
sections.why: Likely reason: the safe rename stops a half-written status file, and the retries handle short locks.
sections.watch_out: An update saved only in memory is lost on restart.

sections.name: JobStore: request_cancellation
sections.title: Cancelling a running job
sections.what: For a job that is queued or running, creates a cancel marker file and sets a message saying cancellation was requested. Finished or failed jobs are returned unchanged.
sections.why: Likely reason: a marker file lets running work notice the request without shared memory.
sections.watch_out: Cancellation takes effect only at the checkpoints where the work looks for the marker, so it is not instant.

sections.name: JobStore: cancelled
sections.title: Single schedule processing and cache
sections.what: Runs one schedule. Computes a cache key from the file and version numbers, applies any saved column mapping, waits for the key's lock, and then reuses a cached parse or parses the file and saves the result. The section label says cancelled, but the code is the middle of the process method.
sections.why: Likely reason: reusing a cached parse saves time when the same file is uploaded again.
sections.watch_out: A cancel request is checked before and during the cache wait, so a cancel during lock waiting stops the job cleanly.

sections.name: JobStore (part 6)
sections.title: Finishing a single schedule job
sections.what: Stores record counts, the project list and cache details, then sets the status to cancelled, mapping required or ready with a matching message. Unexpected errors set the status to failed. Its last lines begin the separate method for combined schedules.
sections.why: Likely reason: the status tells the frontend what to show next.
sections.watch_out: Any unexpected error is saved as failed with its raw text, which may be technical wording for the user.

sections.name: JobStore: cancelled
sections.title: Combining several schedules into one
sections.what: Parses each schedule separately, combines them into one report and database, and marks the job ready. Errors mark it failed, or cancelled if a cancel marker is present.
sections.why: Likely reason: combined runs are treated as fresh work, so no cache is reused.
sections.watch_out: Progress for combined runs only counts records and does not report source bytes, unlike single schedules.

sections.name: new_job_state
sections.title: New job status
sections.what: Creates a fresh queued status for a new job, with the current time and the upload message.
sections.why: Likely reason: every new job starts in the same known state.
sections.watch_out: The message text here is shown to users, so changing it changes what they see.

summary: Keeps the state of each upload job on disk and in memory, and runs schedule processing with progress updates and cancellation.
purpose: Gives the rest of the app one place to create, read, update, cancel and process jobs.
why: Likely reason: saving state to disk lets a job survive page reloads and server restarts.
how: 1. A job folder is created for each upload. 2. Each change to the job is saved to its state file through a temporary file. 3. Processing computes a cache key from the file and version numbers. 4. If a cached result exists it is reused, otherwise the schedule is parsed into a database and a report. 5. The final status is recorded as ready, mapping required, cancelled or failed.
inputs: Uploaded source files, a saved column mapping, cancel marker files, and cached results from earlier runs.
outputs: A state.json file for each job, an ingestion-report.json file, a staging.sqlite3 database, paths to saved model files, and cache entries.
risks: Cancellation works by looking for a file named cancel in the job folder, so deleting that file mid-run changes behaviour. Single schedules use the cache, but combined schedules never do.
debug: Read the job's state.json under the work root. Its message field usually states what happened, and its status field shows where processing stopped.
